quest.title: The Ancient Azure Stars
quest.description: The vast expanse of the starry sky extends endlessly into the distance, with many a fate hidden within. It is simply fascinating: The beautiful sky stands silently in the mirage, its bosom wide and vast, its very existence ancient and gentle, as if it was born to embrace all hankerings after destiny and to grace everyone with its compassion. Mona understands fate in a way similar to this starry sky.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

talks.objective: Follow the hint and explore the area
Return to the mirage and use the shard

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Huh, we've returned here once more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the story's not finished yet. Let the adventure continue!

talks.objective: Return to the mirage and use the shard

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Whoa! Wait, how the...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Another house in Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What are we doing in my house!!!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Your house? This is your house?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: My, how unexpected... I heard Lady Megistus lived a modest life, but this abode...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look at the labels on these books on the ground... "Only one of its kind, 990,000 Mora..." Hey! That's super expensive!

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: There are so many expensive-looking hardcovers over here... So this is what an astrologist's room looks like...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: The rooms are exquisitely designed... This place must be very expensive.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Hey, I'm just occasionally out of Mora, that's all. I never said I was a pauper.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: You're not? Ugh, so what about those times I treated you to meals? And had you over to my place for dinner?

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Ahem! Thou wert blessed with the coveted opportunity to enter the palace of the Immernachtreich and meet with the Kaiser and Kaiserin der Verurteilung. Or hast thou conveniently forgotten this magnificent occasion?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Oh, yes, the stew and cold cuts your mother made were heavenly! Mmm, I could go for some more of that right now...

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Lady Megistus, this is not the time for such things!

response.speaker: Xinyan
response.text: Is that Mondstadt cuisine? I wanna try some! I heard Mondstadt has lots of local delicacies, especially meat dishes.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Hmph, then I shall extend to you the honor of meeting the Kaiser and Kaiserin with me on a future occasion.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Now that you mention it, it has been a while since I visited a friend's house. I shall gladly oblige.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Oh, but shouldn't we bring some sort of gift?

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Those two are very kind and understanding, so please don't worry about that. Just bring yourselves.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: You seriously have to try her mom's cold cut platter. It's her specialty, or something — anyway, it's simply delightful!

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Not to interrupt, but perhaps we should start working on the puzzle at hand? Ever since I entered this place, I have found myself most preoccupied with that ornament...

choices.text: It was my misconception this whole time...

talks.objective: Follow the star to the destination
Follow the star to the destination

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: What a magnificent view...

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Lady Megistus, I believe this is the firmest evidence yet of your immense genius. You truly are the greatest archmage in the history of the Immernachtreich.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Thank you, although the Immernachtreich really doesn't have that much of a history...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: ...Stars like diamonds, and the moon like a pearl. This is the most brilliant night sky I have ever beheld.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: It's beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: To call up such a mirage, Mona must have a vast and boundless sea of stars in her heart.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mona, what's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...I'm just thinking, these must be the things that we aspire to.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: This night sky is incredibly beautiful. In fact, I might go so far as to say it's even more beautiful than what I usually see in divinations.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: All the stars are in their rightful place.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...This is definitely my mirage. Only here can I see extraordinary sights like these.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Extraordinary? Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You know, the night sky of Teyvat is truly marvelous. All the answers in the world seem to have been hidden within.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: "When is my missing son going to be found?"

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: "Do they love me or not?"

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: "Will I ever recover?"

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: As your stars move across the sky, they record all your life events in their path. And among all the people in the world, a considerable number will see their stars deviate from their path.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: When your stars are on track, it means you will be healthy, happy, and at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Conversely, if your stars go off track, everything will get worse.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The starry sky in my divinations would never look as perfect as this. Some stars would lose their way, and others would fall...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...I wish everyone could be happy, and stay on track.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: To this end, I offer advice and tell the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I know it's useless. All fates are already revealed in the night sky, with mine, too, just another among them. I can't change anything.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Even so... outside of astrology, outside of the words of truth, I still cling to the wisp of an irrational fantasy.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: We must all live within the confines of reality, but... call me presumptuous, but I still believe in miracles.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: In this vast sea of stars, there are stars for you, for me, for everybody.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What are the chances of one star encountering another? Are these encounters not the most wonderful miracles in all of destiny? ...I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But within Teyvat, the stars in the sky will always have a place for us. Even if astrology is resolutely rational, fate remains arbitrary, cruel, but romantic.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mona, you seem to have been deep in thought...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you found the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...I think I have figured out what those stars are hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: "Now, I will seize my own destiny."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back here again. So... Are we completely out of the mirage?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: How strange...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: My mirage didn't contain any hints on the Fatui or the machine... Does that mean they had nothing to do with these mirages after all?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Or perhaps these mirages are a mere consequence, and not part of a process at all?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm, Paimon's lost...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I mean, these mirages were not steps towards solving the mystery, but rather a direct effect of whatever is going on.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Someone did something to bring the mirages into being. As they were just passive side products, it was natural that they couldn't provide us with any useful information.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: In other words, those mirages were only about ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hmm, pure materializations of ourselves... Interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Everyone, maybe we should go back to where this whole thing began.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: #During our first day on the island, {NICKNAME} and I checked out the Fatui camp together. We found a strange machine there, as well as some disoriented Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: The researcher who spoke to us claimed that the machine was just a Fatui industrial invention. He even promised to not disturb us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right right, and the cappy-cap guy looked half asleep the entire time. He kept talking nonsense!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I wonder, is it possible that "madness" and "mirages" are two different outcomes of the machine's influence?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: If so, everything can be traced back to that damaged machine — except for the difference in how it affects people. This, I believe, is caused by differences between the affected people themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: When you put it that way... it is indeed difficult to distinguish dreams and hallucinations.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is, the device affected us differently because we are different from the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, and according to our observations over these past few days, I think... the difference is that we all have stronger willpower.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, I can get behind that.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: People with strong willpower will hallucinate instead of falling into madness, but those who break too easily can't maintain a stable mirage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In other words, we should go back to the Fatui camp and destroy that machine right away.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: No, it should be repaired, rather than destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: What mein Fräulein means is that rashly destroying a machine we do not understand may lead to more serious consequences. It would be better to find a way to repair it first.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Right, it pays to be cautious.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: If my guess is correct, that machine is capable of influencing the human brain. So we'd better tread carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So let's go now! There's no time to waste!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I understand the governing laws of the universe, and have glimpsed secrets between heaven and earth. Observing it is enough for me, there's no need to force it to change.
